title: Air Starter Motor Heat Shield Replacement and Duct Standoff Change
abstract: Replaces the obsolete air starter motor heat shield with a current-standard item and moves the duct standoffs clear of the shield edge, a design-frozen change awaiting certification closure before the production cut-in is set.

sections.reason: The delivered heat shield is built from a laminate the supplier withdrew in 2023, and the remaining stock covers production into 2026 only. Rather than requalify the old laminate, the change moves to the current standard shield already used on the auxiliary power unit installation. The opportunity was taken to address a long standing minor finding, where the starter duct standoffs sit on the shield edge and produce local fretting that shows up at every engine change.
sections.description: The heat shield is replaced by the current standard item, which is thinner but carries a higher continuous temperature rating and needs a different fastener spacing at the forward edge. The two duct standoffs are moved fifty-five millimetres inboard onto the existing bracket holes, clear of the shield edge, and the cable ties retaining the starter harness in that area are changed to the current standard so the harness no longer bears on the shield. The starter motor, the start valve and the duct itself are unchanged.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of one point four kilograms per engine. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable, because the fastener spacing at the forward edge differs and the old shield cannot be fitted to the revised standoff arrangement. The removal task changes for the standoff positions. Engine start procedure and dispatch are unaffected, and the crew sees no difference.
sections.embodiment_note: Design is frozen and the certification file is with the authority. Production cut-in will be set when the closure letter is received; no retrofit is planned because the existing shield remains serviceable for the life of the aircraft.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in MSN to be set on certification closure; existing shield stock covers the line until then
